# SMSApp — release-scope reference

SMSApp separates job administration from SMS transport. The web dashboard signs you in with Google, selects one of your registered phones and either its completed contact sync or a CSV, normalizes and previews recipients, snapshots one message, and requires an explicit dispatch action. Supabase (Postgres with row-level security) stores phone, contact, job, recipient, claim and outcome state; queue changes go only through database functions. The selected Android phone performs each SMS send through its configured SIM.

## Release limits

- Distribution: signed APK, "SMS Mobile App", from https://smsapp.aoneahsan.com/apps#download (not on Google Play); it runs on Supabase
- Android application ID: `com.aoneahsan.smsapp`.
- Sender: one of your own registered Android phones per job.
- Enrollment: off by default and explicitly enabled on the phone.
- SIM: one configured default SMS subscription; no per-job dual-SIM selector.
- Contacts: permission plus a separate owner-initiated device-scoped cloud sync.
- CSV: UTF-8, recognized phone header, at most 5 MiB.
- Job: one message and at most 5,000 unique eligible destinations; plan limits apply on top (Free: 100 recipients per job and 100 messages a month; Pro and Family: 5,000 per job, no monthly cap).
- Send rate: set per job, in messages per second, minute or hour.

## Destination safety

The release accepts only ordinary Pakistani mobile destinations in the `030`–`036` ranges. Unambiguous `03…`, `923…`, `00923…`, and `+923…` values normalize to E.164. Foreign numbers, landlines, short codes, service or premium destinations, malformed values, and unknown ranges are excluded. The policy runs at import, persistence/release, and Android dispatch, with no override.

The prefix policy cannot prove recipient consent, number ownership, service availability, account balance, tariff, package inclusion, or delivery. The sender remains responsible for lawful sending and carrier charges.

## Result semantics

Pending means not yet dispatched. A claim assigns a bounded lease to the selected phone. Sent means Android returned successful sent callbacks for the message parts; it is not a delivery guarantee. A confirmed error becomes failed. If Android may have accepted the message but the result cannot be proved, the outcome is uncertain and must not be automatically retried.

## Privacy and platform boundaries

SMSApp is send-only. It does not read or upload received SMS, call logs, location, advertising identifiers, or legacy external-storage contents. It is not a default SMS handler. There is no cloud SMS gateway, public phone pool, desktop sender, or npm product in this milestone. iOS: removed 2026-10-30 — re-add when an Apple Developer account exists.

## White-label & licensing

A business can license SMS Mobile App to run under its own name, or buy it outright. With a licence we host and deploy it, connect the buyer's domain and apply their name, logo and colours; no source code changes hands, and the product stays available to other buyers until a buyout. The licence covers the Android app (the buyer's own signed APK, installed from their site and updated over the air, never through Google Play) with the web dashboard and backend. There is no iOS build. Six months of updates are included; renewals run 3, 6 or 12 months. A buyout hands over the source of every repository that builds the product, and it is then sold to nobody else. Each deployment serves /.well-known/smsapp-white-label-license.json, checkable at https://smsapp.aoneahsan.com/verify-license. Prices: https://smsapp.aoneahsan.com/white-label/pricing. Guide: https://smsapp-docs.aoneahsan.com/white-label
